title: Agent Platforms & Harnesses
description: The layer other agents on this site are often built on: platforms for building, orchestrating, and running multiple AI agents together, rather than a single-purpose product of their own.

title: Source of Truth
description: Agents need a reliable, structured record of what the network is supposed to look like before they can safely act on it. These are the inventory and intent-modeling platforms that play that role, plus the MCP servers that expose them to agents.

title: Observability & Telemetry
description: Monitoring and metrics platforms, and the MCP servers or protocol bridges that let an agent query them directly instead of working from a stale dashboard export.

title: Orchestration & Execution
description: The layer where an agent's decision actually turns into a change on a device: task orchestration platforms and the MCP bridges that carry real write and execute capability, not just read access.

title: Network Assurance & Digital Twins
description: Platforms that model network behavior end to end, so a proposed change can be verified against a simulated or mathematically modeled version of the network before it touches production.

title: AI Security
description: The threat models, hardening patterns, and access-control tooling specific to giving an agent real access to network infrastructure, distinct from traditional network security.

title: Standards & Protocols
description: The protocols and frameworks agentic networking is being built on, from the Model Context Protocol itself to early-stage IETF drafts and industry autonomy frameworks. Where something is a draft rather than an adopted standard, that's called out rather than implied.

title: Lab & Test Tooling
description: Sandboxes and lab environments built for trying an agent against network gear without risking anything real.

title: Community & Further Reading
description: Looser than the other categories by design: foundational reading for agent builders alongside the communities and venues where agentic networking is actively discussed.
